tutorial.title: Welcome to Aurion

intro.body: You lead a nation, then a civilisation. Time runs in weeks and you can stop it whenever you like. Here is where things are: it takes under a minute.

tutorial.footerNote: Press Esc to move to the next step.

hud.title: Your vital signs
hud.body: Date, treasury, popularity and your civilisation's level on the Kardashev scale. Click a number to open the system behind it.

map.title: The world
map.body: Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom. Your nation has the gold border. Click a country to see who they are and what you can do; the labels flag what is happening.

panels.title: The eight systems
panels.body: Economy, Research, Military, Intelligence, Diplomacy, Internal politics, UN and Cosmos. One click opens the panel, another closes it. A dot means something needs you.

speed.title: Time is yours
speed.body: Pause, 1×, 2×, 4×. The space bar pauses and resumes. When a decision arrives, time stops by itself.

outro.title: Over to you
outro.body: Start from the briefing: begin a research and your first megaproject. Govern well.

intro.title: Welcome to Aurion
intro.body: You lead a nation, then a civilisation. Time runs in weeks and you can stop it whenever you like. Here is where things are: it takes under a minute.

cosmos.title: The long game
cosmos.body: In Cosmos you start megaprojects: from the power grid to the Moon, Mars and a Dyson sphere. Each one makes your civilisation stronger, for good.

views.title: Other worlds
views.body: Switch from Earth to the Moon, Mars and the solar-system map: see where your projects stand and, once you have colonies, decide what they send home.

briefing.title: The briefing
briefing.body: Suggested next steps on top, dispatches below: decisions, wars and treaties, covert operations, UN votes and your rivals' progress in the space race.

earth_smart_grid.name: Continental power grid

earth_arcologies.name: Arcologies
earth_arcologies.desc: Self-sufficient vertical cities that free up land and lift morale.

earth_fusion.name: Fusion reactor

earth_spaceport.name: Spaceport
earth_spaceport.desc: The launch pad to everything else. Needs your first space technology.

orbit_elevator.name: Space elevator

moon_base.name: Lunar base
moon_base.desc: The first permanent settlement beyond Earth.

moon_helium3.name: Helium-3 mines

moon_mass_driver.name: Mass driver

endScreen.continueHint: The game goes on with no ending: victories become milestones.

odyssey.name: Odyssey
odyssey.pitch: The long game: from your capital to the first colony among the stars.
odyssey.do: You govern with no finish line to end the game. Economy, alliances and research all feed the megaprojects that take your civilisation to orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond.
odyssey.win: There's no victory screen: every victory condition becomes a milestone to collect. The real aim is the Kardashev scale: Type I, Type II, the first interstellar colony.
odyssey.lose: By collapse: popularity on the floor, bankruptcy, your capital occupied or every faction against you.
odyssey.length: Many hours. It saves itself: pick it up whenever you like.
odyssey.forWho: For players who want to see how far they can go. The recommended way to get to know Aurion.
odyssey.changes: No victory to choose: you go straight from nation to difficulty.
odyssey.goal: Climb the Kardashev scale. Victories are milestones: the game doesn't end.

campaign.name: Campaign
campaign.pitch: One goal, chosen by you. Reach it and you've won.
campaign.do: You pick one road to victory and bend everything else to it: every decision is judged by how much closer it gets you.
campaign.win: By reaching your chosen goal: economic, diplomatic, scientific, military, total domination or Ascension (Kardashev Type I).
campaign.lose: By collapse: popularity on the floor, bankruptcy, your capital occupied or every faction against you.
campaign.length: One to two hours, depending on the goal and the world.
campaign.forWho: For players who want a game with a beginning and an end, or to try one playstyle at a time.
campaign.changes: Adds a step: after the nation you choose your road to victory.
campaign.goal: Reach the goal you chose: the game ends there, in victory.

spaceRace.name: Space Race
spaceRace.pitch: A straight race: first to complete the Planetary Grid wins.
spaceRace.do: Everything serves one thing: space research, treasury and construction sites to reach the Planetary Grid before the rival nations racing alongside you.
spaceRace.win: By being first to complete the Planetary Grid, the megaproject that takes a civilisation to Kardashev Type I.
spaceRace.lose: If a rival nation completes the Planetary Grid before you. Or by collapse, as in every mode.
spaceRace.length: A few hours, with rivals on your heels from start to finish.
spaceRace.forWho: For players who love a race and a tight build order.
spaceRace.changes: No victory to choose: the goal is already set.
spaceRace.goal: Complete the Planetary Grid before your rivals. If they get there first, you lose.

throne.name: Throne
throne.pitch: Climb onto the podium of economies and hold it for ten years.
throne.do: You take your nation into the world's top three economies, then defend the spot. You have ten years to get there the first time; from then on every week on the podium counts toward victory.
throne.win: Ten years on the podium of economies, in total.
throne.lose: Ten years without ever reaching the podium, or five straight years off it once you have been there. Where blocs exist, also five years as a pariah in all of them. Or by collapse.
throne.length: A few hours. The pressure never lets up, not even when you're ahead.
throne.forWho: For players who want constant pressure and already know how to grow an economy.
throne.changes: No victory to choose. A nation with an already solid economy helps: check the ranking in the “Nation” step.
throne.goal: Reach the top three economies within ten years and stay there for ten years in total.
throne.noteIsolation: In this world the pariah defeat applies too: reputation below −50 in every bloc for five years in a row.
throne.noteNoIsolation: In this world the pariah defeat doesn't apply: only the economic podium counts.

chronicles.name: Chronicles
chronicles.pitch: History in chapters: you play through the world's eras, with a recap between each.
chronicles.do: You play the chosen world's historical eras, one after another. At each change of era the game pauses to show how the world has changed and where you stand.
chronicles.win: By still being in power at the end of the last era. Achieve Total domination before that and the story closes there, in victory.
chronicles.lose: By collapse, in any era: popularity on the floor, bankruptcy, your capital occupied or every faction against you.
chronicles.length: A long game, but with natural places to stop: the end of each era.
chronicles.forWho: For players who'd rather have a story with its own rhythm than a race to a goal.
chronicles.changes: Limits the choice of world to those with historical eras. No victory to choose.
chronicles.goal: Stay in power until the end of the last era.
chronicles.note: Only played in worlds with historical eras: {worlds}. If your plan had a different one, it switches to {world}: you can change it in the next step.

guide.title: How to play
guide.lead: Everything you need to know, in seven sections to skim. Nothing you couldn't also learn by playing.

goal.title: In short
goal.body: You run a nation. Time passes in weeks and can always be stopped: pause, decide, resume. With a few levers — taxes, research, alliances, spies, the army — you grow the country and hold it together; with what's left over you build the megaprojects that take your civilisation off Earth.

glance.title: One planet, one glance
glance.body: What's happening is on the globe: wars, alliances, construction. If something needs a decision from you, the briefing says so.

levers.title: Few levers, big effects
levers.body: Every action states its price and its effect before the click. You don't need to micromanage: you need to choose.

long.title: The long game
long.body: From the power grid to the Dyson sphere: megaprojects are the road, the Kardashev scale is the odometer.

goal.tip: If it's your first time, start with Quick play: six nations, a one-minute tutorial and no mistake you can't recover from.

modes.title: The five modes
modes.lead: You choose the mode first, because it decides how the game ends.
modes.cta: Length, who it's for and what changes in the following steps: it's all in the first step of a new game.

screen.title: The game screen
screen.lead: The planet fills the screen. Everything else floats over it, always in the same place.
screen.diagramLabel: Diagram of the game screen: status bar on top, systems on the left, briefing on the right, planet in the centre, views at the bottom.

hud.name: Status bar.
hud.body: On top: date, treasury, popularity, Kardashev rating and the time controls.

dock.name: Systems.
dock.body: On the left: the eight systems of government. A click, or keys 1 to 8, opens the panel beside it.

stage.name: Stage.
stage.body: The world you're looking at. Drag to rotate it, click a nation to select it.

briefing.name: Briefing.
briefing.body: On the right: what needs your attention right now, and the latest news.

views.name: Views.
views.body: At the bottom: switch from Earth to the Moon, Mars and the Solar system. A world opens once you complete your first project there.

card.name: Nation card.
card.body: Appears when you select a nation: the essential numbers and quick actions towards it.

systems.title: The eight systems
systems.lead: Each has its own panel and its own key. For each: what it's for, and one practical tip.

economy.name: Economy
economy.what: Taxes, trade and investment: the system that pays for all the others. The treasury moves every week with your income, and the breakdown says where every euro comes from.
economy.tip: Invest little and often. A sum that is large next to your GDP, or many investments close together, return less euro for euro: the full return comes back after a few months.

research.name: Research
research.what: One technology at a time, across four branches: civil, military, intelligence and space. Each discovery unlocks new actions or permanent bonuses.
research.tip: Never leave the labs idle: when a project finishes, pick the next one straight away.

military.name: Military
military.what: Army, navy and air force, and where to deploy them. Every war keeps a score: it rises by winning battles, by occupying the enemy's region and, slowly, simply by being stronger.
military.tip: Peace is signed on the score's terms: under 20 it is a draw, from 20 the side ahead collects reparations, from 60 the other capitulates. Every week of war costs approval: do not drag it out.

intel.name: Intelligence
intel.what: Spies and counter-intelligence: stealing technology, sabotage, propaganda, destabilising a government, striking a key figure. The target you pick changes the effect, and rivals send agents after you too.
intel.tip: An agent comes home when the mission ends, unless caught: then you lose them and relations drop by 12. Counter-intelligence is what stops, or exposes, the operations against you.

diplomacy.name: Diplomacy
diplomacy.what: Your relations with every nation: trade deals, alliances, sanctions, declarations of war and peace treaties.
diplomacy.tip: An alliance takes preparation: improve relations first, and propose it only when the other nation thinks well of you. Each ally also takes 4% off the price of megaprojects.

politics.name: Internal politics
politics.what: Popularity and five factions, each with its weight and a lever of its own: the army combat power, business income, the clergy approval, populists growth, reformists research.
politics.tip: A faction at 70% or more is behind you and gives a bonus; at 30% or less it works against you. Choose which to keep close by what you are trying to do.

un.name: UN
un.what: Resolutions to vote on and to propose. Where there's a Council, permanent members hold a veto. How you vote shifts your reputation with the blocs.
un.tip: Before voting, look at who the resolution targets: a vote against an ally has a price.

cosmos.name: Cosmos
cosmos.what: The megaprojects, from the power grid to the Proxima colony. You pay up front, they take weeks, and they pay back forever.
cosmos.tip: Open your first construction site early: the Continental power grid is cheap and lifts GDP for the whole game.

cosmos.title: Kardashev and megaprojects
cosmos.lead: The Kardashev scale measures how much energy a civilisation controls. You start at 0.70 and climb by completing megaprojects, in seven stages.

cost.title: You pay up front.
cost.body: The cost leaves the treasury at the start and scales with your starting economy: the same project weighs the same for a small nation and a superpower.

time.title: It takes weeks.
time.body: Ten for the first projects, several years for the last. Meanwhile the world moves on.

sites.title: One site at a time.
sites.body: At first you build one project at a time. The Orbital shipyard, the Mass driver and Ceres station each add one more site.

tech.title: It needs space research.
tech.body: Some stages need a share of the space technologies: your first discovery for the Spaceport, 40% for the Moon, 70% for Mars.

rivals.title: Rivals race you.
rivals.body: Other nations climb the same ladder. Whoever completes a project first takes the record, and the prestige that comes with it.

cancel.title: You can cancel.
cancel.body: Stopping a build returns half of what you paid.

colonies.title: Bases become colonies.
colonies.body: On the Moon and Mars the population grows by itself toward the room your projects provide. You give each colony a mandate — science, industry or trade — that decides what it sends home every week.

land.title: Land has to be taken.
land.body: The Moon and Mars are divided into twenty sectors. You start from the one your base stands on and expand into its neighbours; each sector takes two structures — habitat, laboratory, mine, foundry. Rivals claim land too, and there is not enough for everyone.

cosmos.tip: Bonuses are permanent and they stack: every project that lifts GDP makes the next one easier to afford.

lose.title: How you lose
lose.lead: Four ways, the same in every mode. None comes out of the blue: there's always a countdown.

popularity.title: Popularity collapse
popularity.body: Popularity stays below 10% for twelve weeks in a row.
popularity.avoid: lower taxes, placate the factions that matter most, end the wars you aren't winning.

bankruptcy.title: Bankruptcy
bankruptcy.body: The treasury stays in the red for twenty-six weeks in a row.
bankruptcy.avoid: cut spending before you go below zero. In the red you also lose popularity, every week.

capital.title: Capital occupied
capital.body: Enemy forces larger than yours stay in your capital's region for twenty-six weeks.
capital.avoid: don't empty the homeland for campaigns abroad, and sue for peace when the war turns against you.

factions.title: Every faction hostile
factions.body: All five factions stay below 20 satisfaction for twelve weeks.
factions.avoid: keeping one on your side is enough. Pick the most influential and don't lose it.

lose.note: These timings are for Normal difficulty: they can be longer on Easy and get shorter on Hard and in Iron Man. Space Race and Throne add a defeat of their own, described under the modes.

keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keys.lead: Everything can also be done from the keyboard alone: Tab moves through the controls, Enter activates them.

trend.collecting: The income chart draws itself week by week: let time run.
trend.aria: Income over the last {weeks} weeks: from {from} to {to}

warning.inTheRed: The treasury has been in the red {weeks, plural, =0 {since this week} =1 {for one week} other {for # weeks}}. After {limit} straight weeks below zero the government falls: you have {left, plural, =1 {one left} other {# left}}. While you stay in the red you also lose half a popularity point a week.
warning.runway: You are spending more than you earn: at this pace the treasury runs dry in {weeks, plural, =0 {under a week} =1 {one week} other {# weeks}}. {limit} straight weeks below zero and the game is lost.

sources.sanctions: {n, plural, =1 {One sanction in force} other {# sanctions in force}}

sources.coloniesHint: What your colonies on other worlds send home
sources.factionsHintLoyal: They are behind you: they pay in more
sources.factionsHintHostile: They are against you: they hide their money

tax.title: Tax policy
tax.label: Tax rate
tax.reactions: How the factions take it (satisfaction points)
tax.tradeOff: More tax, more income. But each extra point costs Business 0.4 satisfaction and gives Populists 0.3 and Reformists 0.1; Military and Clergy barely notice. And popularity follows the factions. Move the slider to see the bill.

invest.title: Investments
invest.intro: You pay once, up front. The effect stays.

economy.name: Economy
economy.rate: Up to 4 euros of GDP per euro

infra.name: Infrastructure
infra.rate: Up to 2 euros of GDP per euro, plus popularity

invest.shareHint: Share of today's treasury. Sums that are large next to your GDP return less, euro for euro.

blocked.empty: The treasury is empty: there is nothing to invest.
blocked.enter: Type the amount, in millions of euros.
blocked.invalid: The amount must be a number above zero.
blocked.tooMuch: That is more than you have in the treasury ({treasury}).

preview.title: What you get
preview.income: Income {gain} a week: pays for itself in {weeks, plural, =1 {one week} other {# weeks}}
preview.incomeNone: No income gain at the current tax rate
preview.research: Research from {from} to {to} points a week, for good
preview.spies: {n, plural, =0 {No new spy (they cost € 50M each)} =1 {One new spy: {total} in all} other {# new spies: {total} in all}}
preview.saturated: It returns {pct} of the usual: the sum is large next to your GDP, or you have invested a lot lately. Smaller sums, spaced out, return more.

sectors.title: What the country lives on
sectors.note: Every 10 points of Services lift the tax take by {services}%, every 10 of Technology by {tech}%. Agriculture and Industry make GDP but pay no extra tax.

mega.title: Megaprojects
mega.building: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing under construction} =1 {One project under construction} other {# projects under construction}}
mega.none: Nothing to start right now: see what is missing in Cosmos

invest.invalidAmount: That is not a valid amount to invest.
invest.insufficientTreasury: The treasury cannot cover this investment.

tax.outOfRange: The tax rate must be between 0 and 100%.

country.notFound: Your country is no longer in play.

hero.idleHint: This week’s research points are wasted until you pick something to study.
hero.weeksUnit: {weeks, plural, =0 {ready this week} =1 {week to discovery} other {weeks to discovery}}
hero.allDoneHint: This scenario’s tree is complete. From here, science means megaprojects.

branchHint.space: The road to orbit, the Moon and Mars.

recommended.label: Recommended
recommended.reason: {weeks, plural, =1 {One week} other {# weeks}} of work{opens, plural, =0 {} =1 {, and it opens the way to one more technology} other {, and it opens the way to # more technologies}}.
recommended.reasonNoOutput: {opens, plural, =0 {The cheapest one available.} =1 {It opens the way to one more technology.} other {It opens the way to # more technologies.}}

panelResearch.startCost: {points} points: about {weeks, plural, =1 {one week} other {# weeks}} at {output} points a week
panelResearch.startCostNoOutput: {points} points. You produce none today: it will not advance.
panelResearch.rules: One project at a time, no queue: once started it cannot be stopped, and you pick the next when it is done.
panelResearch.rulesNoOutput: You produce no research points: invest in Research from the Economy panel to get the labs moving.

tree.title: Tech tree
tree.empty: This scenario has no technologies in this branch.

eta.weeks: {weeks, plural, =0 {Ready this week.} =1 {Ready in one week.} other {Ready in # weeks.}}
eta.never: Stalled: you produce no research points.

blocked.busyWeeks: The labs are busy with {name}: you can start this in {weeks, plural, =0 {a few days} =1 {one week} other {# weeks}}.

milestone.badge: A world first is at stake
milestone.open: Still unclaimed: whoever gets here first earns {first} reputation in every bloc, followers earn {follow}.
milestone.yours: The first is yours since week {week}: {first} reputation in every bloc.
milestone.taken: {country} got here first, in week {week}. You can still earn {follow} reputation.

space.title: Space technology
space.why: You hold {pct}% of the branch. That share is what opens the megaprojects beyond Earth:
space.gateMissing: {n, plural, =1 {1 technology to go} other {# technologies to go}}

firsts.title: World firsts
firsts.intro: Whoever reaches these first earns reputation in every bloc. Followers get far less.

research.techNotFound: That technology does not exist in this scenario.
research.alreadyActive: The labs are already working on something else.
research.missingPrereq: The technologies that come before it are still missing.

country.notFound: Your country is no longer in play.

hero.settles: With today’s factions it settles around {pct} (the white tick). Popularity chases the factions’ mood, weighted by influence, and drifts slowly back towards 50%.

danger.title: How a government falls
danger.popularity: Popularity below {pct}% for {weeks} weeks in a row.
danger.popularityActive: You have been below {pct}% {weeks, plural, =0 {since this week} =1 {for one week} other {for # weeks}}: {left, plural, =1 {one more} other {# more}} and the government falls. Make a concession to the heaviest faction now.
danger.factions: All five factions below {pct}% for {weeks} weeks in a row. {hostile, plural, =0 {None is hostile today.} =1 {One is hostile today.} other {# are hostile today.}}
danger.factionsActive: Every faction has been below {pct}% {weeks, plural, =0 {since this week} =1 {for one week} other {for # weeks}}: {left, plural, =1 {one more} other {# more}} and they overthrow you. Lifting a single one above the line stops the clock.

democracy.name: Democracy
democracy.desc: You rule by consent: reformists, business and populists feel represented.

autocracy.name: Autocracy
autocracy.desc: Power sits in a few hands: the military is at home, reformists chafe.

oligarchy.name: Oligarchy
oligarchy.desc: Big money decides: business thrives, populists nurse a grudge.

theocracy.name: Theocracy
theocracy.desc: Law follows faith: the clergy at the centre, reformists at the edge.

monarchy.name: Monarchy
monarchy.desc: The crown rests on army and clergy; populists get little room.

army.name: Military
army.wants: General staff and veterans. They want a strong government; taxes barely touch them.

business.name: Business
business.wants: Industry and finance. They want low taxes: nobody reacts to the tax rate like they do.

religious.name: Clergy
religious.wants: The religious authorities. They want a government close to the faith; taxes barely touch them.

populist.name: Populists
populist.wants: The street. They want high taxes, which they read as redistribution.

reformist.name: Reformists
reformist.wants: Universities and the urban class. They want an open country and like taxes a little higher.

factions.title: Factions
factions.intro: A concession costs {cost} and lifts one faction’s satisfaction by {points} points at once. The more a faction weighs, the more it moves popularity.

placate.maxed: Satisfaction is already at the top: a concession would be wasted.
placate.blocked: A concession costs {cost}: you have {treasury}. Raise your income from the Economy panel.

moves.title: What moves them
moves.taxDown: Taxes: each extra point of tax costs {points} satisfaction.
moves.taxUp: Taxes: each extra point of tax is worth {points} satisfaction.
moves.governmentDown: {government}: it holds them back, −{points} per week.
moves.drift: Left alone they drift back to 50%: {points} this week.

news.title: Political news
news.empty: No political news so far. Strikes, scandals and reforms will show up here.

placate.insufficientTreasury: The treasury cannot cover a concession.

country.notFound: Your country is no longer in play.

hero.label: Your standing in the world
hero.wars: {n, plural, =1 {1 war under way} other {# wars under way}}
hero.goalCoverage: Goal: ally with {pct} of all nations
hero.goalControl: Goal: a front of {n} nations, yours included
hero.tensionHint: World tension rises by 5 for every war under way and by 1 for every sanctions regime or recently exposed spy.

pick.title: Pick a nation
pick.body: Tap it on the globe or in the list below to see what it thinks of you and what you can offer.

dossier.label: Relations with {name}
dossier.unknown: GDP and army stay unknown until you have reliable sources in the country.

effect.proposeAlliance: They accept unless they are hostile. Attitude +20; an ally cannot be attacked, opens its borders to your troops and counts toward victory.
effect.breakAlliance: Attitude −30. It no longer counts toward victory and closes its borders to your troops.
effect.tradeDeal: Attitude +10 and 2% more income for both sides: about {gain} a week for you. Only a war dissolves it.
effect.imposeSanction: Attitude −25. Takes 5% of income from both sides (about {loss} a week from you), raises world tension by 1 and gives you grounds for war.
effect.liftSanction: Attitude +10. You recover about {gain} a week and world tension drops by 1.
effect.declareWar: Attitude −50, alliances and trade deals are torn up, world tension +5. Keeping the army at war costs you about {cost} a week.
effect.sueForPeace: The war ends at once. Attitude +15, world tension −5 and you save about {saving} a week.

breakAlliance.title: Break the alliance?
breakAlliance.description: Their attitude toward you drops by 30 and the ally no longer counts toward victory. To ally again it must climb back to at least 0.

declareWar.title: Declare war?
declareWar.description: Attitude −50, trade deals end, world tension +5 and a weekly cost for every garrisoned unit. The war lasts until either side makes peace.

sueForPeace.title: Make peace?
sueForPeace.description: The war ends at once and their attitude recovers by 15. Troops already deployed stay where they are.

error.atWar: You are at war: make peace first.
error.attitudeTooLow: They are hostile to you: attitude must be 0 or higher.
error.noAlliance: There is no alliance to break.
error.notSanctioned: There are no sanctions to lift.
error.alreadyTrading: You already have a trade deal.
error.alliedCannotWar: You cannot attack an ally: break the alliance first.
error.nonAggressionPact: A non-aggression pact binds you: war is off the table.
error.attitudeTooHighForWar: No casus belli: attitude must be −25 or worse, or sanctions must be in force.

bloc.notAvailable: There are no blocs in this scenario.
bloc.alreadyMember: You are already a member of this bloc.
bloc.notMember: You are not a member of any bloc.

error.truce: A truce is in force after the last peace: you cannot go back to war yet.

blocs.title: Blocs
blocs.intro: Your bloc backs your UN proposals. Reputation collapses if you use nuclear weapons, grows with disarmament and space firsts, and drifts half a point back toward zero every week.
blocs.empty: No nation belongs to it for now.

join.title: Join the bloc?
join.description: Membership is immediate. As a member, the bloc backs your UN proposals.
join.switch: You leave your current bloc and join the new one at once; from now on it backs your UN proposals.

leave.title: Leave the bloc?
leave.description: You become unaligned: no bloc will back your UN proposals any more. You can rejoin whenever you like.

peace.white: Neither side is far enough ahead to dictate terms: a peace with no winner and no reparations, and attitude recovers by 15. A two-year truce follows.
peace.winReparations: You are winning: {name} pays you {amount} in reparations and your approval rises by 3. At a score of +60 you could force a capitulation. A two-year truce follows.
peace.winCapitulation: {name} capitulates: it pays you {amount} in reparations, hands over {gdp} of GDP and your approval rises by 6. A two-year truce follows.
peace.loseReparations: You are losing: peace costs you {amount} in reparations to {name} and 4 points of approval. If the score reaches −60 the terms get worse. A two-year truce follows.
peace.loseCapitulation: This is a capitulation: you pay {amount} in reparations to {name}, give up {gdp} of GDP and your approval falls by 10. A two-year truce follows.

short.white: a peace with no winner and no reparations.
short.winCapitulation: {name} capitulates: {amount} and {gdp} of GDP for you.
short.loseCapitulation: you capitulate: you pay {amount} and give up {gdp} of GDP.

hero.label: Your armed forces
hero.upkeep: The wars under way cost you {cost} a week: 50 per garrisoned unit, per war.

wars.title: Wars under way
wars.empty: Declaring war takes an attitude of −25 or worse, or sanctions in force.
wars.balanceLabel: You hold {pct} of the forces in the field
wars.noContact: No contact: fighting only happens where both of you have troops in the same region.
wars.howItEnds: The score rises by winning battles, occupying their region and, slowly, simply by being stronger; every week of war costs both sides approval. Peace is signed on the score's terms: under 20 it is a draw, from 20 the side ahead collects reparations, from 60 the other capitulates. If enemy troops in your region outnumber your defenders for 26 weeks in a row, you lose the game.
wars.capitalThreat: {enemy} enemy units are in your region, against {own} defenders. If they outnumber you for {limit} weeks running you lose the game.
wars.capitalFallen: The capital has been overrun for {weeks, plural, =1 {1 week} other {# weeks}}: at {limit} you lose the game. Recruit units or make peace.
wars.scoreLabel: War score {score} on a scale from −100 to +100; 20 earns reparations, 60 a capitulation
wars.toll: {weeks, plural, =0 {Just broken out} =1 {1 week of war} other {# weeks of war}} · losses: {own} yours, {foe} theirs

balance.title: Balance of power
balance.hint: Strength counts garrison and deployed troops: it is the sum that decides battles. Values marked ≈ are estimates; exact figures take at least partial intel.

deploy.title: Deploy troops
deploy.intro: Units leave the garrison and stay in the region: they cannot be recalled. Every week they fight any enemy present in the same region.

access.closed: Closed: needs an alliance or a war with {name}

deploy.pickRegion: Pick a region above, or a nation on the globe.
deploy.noAccess: Region closed: it takes an alliance or a war with {name}.
deploy.noUnits: The garrison is empty: recruit new units.

deployed.title: Deployed troops
deployed.empty: All your units are in garrison.
deployed.age: {weeks, plural, =0 {Just arrived} =1 {In place for 1 week} other {In place for # weeks}}

recruit.title: Recruit
recruit.noFunds: The treasury cannot pay for even one unit.
recruit.tooLittle: Raise the share to recruit at least one unit.

deterrent.hint: As long as you hold one warhead, anyone watching you with enough intel thinks twice before declaring war on you.

arsenal.productionNext: {weeks, plural, =1 {next warhead in 1 week} other {next warhead in # weeks}}
arsenal.noWarheads: You have no warheads to launch.

tactical.title: Tactical strike — one region
tactical.units: Destroys every unit deployed in the region, yours included.
tactical.host: The country that controls the region loses 30 popularity.
tactical.world: World tension +30 and reputation −50 with every bloc. Uses one warhead.
tactical.noTargets: No enemy region: you can only strike where a country you are at war with is based or has troops.

strategic.title: Strategic strike — one nation
strategic.target: The target loses half its GDP and 70% of its treasury; popularity to zero, deployed troops wiped out.
strategic.mad: If it holds warheads it answers: mutual destruction. Both of you lose 80% of GDP, the whole treasury and all popularity; the rest of the world loses 30% of GDP.
strategic.world: World tension +60 and reputation −100 with every bloc. Uses one warhead.
strategic.noTargets: No target: you can only strike a country you are at war with.

dismantle.title: Disarmament
dismantle.noBlocs: In this scenario disarmament earns no reputation: it only shrinks the arsenal.
dismantle.boostFull: A non-proliferation treaty is in force: every warhead dismantled is worth +{perWarhead} reputation with every bloc.
dismantle.boostHalved: Every warhead dismantled is worth +{perWarhead} reputation with every bloc; +{full} once the UN passes a non-proliferation treaty.

confirm.title: Dismantle the warheads?
confirm.description: Dismantled warheads do not come back. Empty the arsenal and you lose your deterrent.

deploy.invalidUnits: Say how many units to deploy.
deploy.notEnoughUnits: You do not have enough units in garrison.
deploy.foreignRegionNoAccess: That region is closed: it takes an alliance or a war with whoever controls it.

nuclear.regionNotEnemy: You can only strike regions where a country you are at war with is based or has troops.
nuclear.targetNotEnemy: You can only strike a country you are at war with.
nuclear.invalidCount: Say how many warheads to dismantle.
nuclear.tooMany: You do not have that many warheads.

network.label: Your network
network.inField: {n, plural, =0 {None in the field} =1 {1 in the field} other {# in the field}}
network.counterIntelHint: Takes {points} points off the success of operations against you and adds them to the risk of their exposure.
network.recruit: An agent comes home when the mission ends, unless caught. Recruiting one costs {cost} invested in intelligence.

pick.title: Pick a target
pick.body: Tap a nation on the globe or in the list at the bottom to open its file and plan an operation.

dossier.label: File on {name}
dossier.howToLearn: To learn more: a successful operation raises the level by one; a trade deal brings at least rumours, an alliance partial sources; idle agents investigate on their own, slowly.

intelDetail.none: No source on the ground. Operations start with no edge and the country's figures remain estimates.
intelDetail.rumors: Unverified rumours: 5 points more success, 5 less risk. The country's figures remain estimates.
intelDetail.partial: Reliable sources: 15 points more success, 15 less risk. You see GDP, army, defences and nuclear arsenal.
intelDetail.full: Nothing escapes you: 25 points more success, 25 less risk, and every figure exact.

composer.title: Plan an operation
composer.detectedEffect: the agent is lost, relations with them worsen by {penalty} and world tension rises by 1 for ten weeks. If the operation had worked, the effect stands.
composer.agentLost: If nobody catches you, the agent comes home when the operation ends, whether it worked or not.
composer.allLocked: No operation is possible against this country for now.
composer.noStealable: Nothing to take: {name} has no technology you lack
composer.done: {op} against {name} under way: outcome in {weeks} weeks.

outcome.steal_tech: the technology is yours at once, with all its effects.

sabotage.economy: their GDP drops by {pct}: that is how much this sector weighs in their economy.
sabotage.science: their research loses 1 point a week.
sabotage.economyUnknown: their GDP drops by 1% to 6%: the bigger the sector, the deeper the cut. Better intel would tell you how much.

outcome.destabilize: the satisfaction of every one of their factions drops by 5.

propaganda.faction: the satisfaction of {faction} drops by 15 and the government's popularity by 2.

assassinate.head_of_state: their government's popularity drops by 10 and every faction loses 5 satisfaction.
assassinate.defence_minister: their military doctrine loses 15% and the military faction loses 10 satisfaction.
assassinate.intelligence_chief: their counter-intelligence loses 10 points and their files are yours: full intel on the country.

active.title: Operations under way
active.eta: {weeks, plural, =0 {Outcome due} =1 {Outcome in 1 week} other {Outcome in # weeks}}

reports.title: Reports
reports.empty: No reports yet: the outcome of each operation lands here.
reports.completed: {op} against {name} succeeded. The agent is home.
reports.failed: {op} against {name} failed: no effect, nobody noticed. The agent is home.
reports.detected: {op} against {name} failed and was exposed: agent lost, relations −{penalty}.
reports.detectedButDone: {op} against {name} worked but was exposed: the effect stands, the agent is lost, relations −{penalty}.
reports.caught: You foiled an operation by {name} against you: {op}. No damage, relations −{penalty}.
reports.when: {weeks, plural, =0 {This week} =1 {1 week ago} other {# weeks ago}}
reports.caughtButDone: {op} by {name} against you: exposed too late, the damage is done. Relations −{penalty}.
reports.hitUnknown: You were hit by an operation: {op}. Sender unknown. Stronger counter-intelligence would have stopped or exposed it.

list.title: What you know about each nation
list.running: {n, plural, =1 {1 operation under way} other {# operations under way}}

error.typeLocked: That operation needs a technology you do not have yet.

panelUN.title: United Nations

hero.label: On the floor
hero.onFloor: {n, plural, =0 {no resolution on the floor} =1 {1 resolution on the floor} other {# resolutions on the floor}}
hero.seatCouncil: You sit on the council: you can veto and table any kind of resolution.
hero.seatAssembly: You vote on everything and can table humanitarian aid and climate accords. Vetoes and other proposals belong to the council.

inactive.title: There is no UN here
inactive.body: This scenario has no council: no resolutions, no votes. In the larger scenarios this is where the world is counted.

panelUN.empty: No resolution on the floor. One arrives when a council member tables it — or when you do.
panelUN.weeksRemaining: {n, plural, =0 {less than a week} =1 {1 week} other {# weeks}}

tally.pending: {n, plural, =1 {1 yet to vote} other {# yet to vote}}

effects.none: no direct effect; it stays on the record as a statement.
effects.treaty: the non-proliferation treaty comes into force: every warhead dismantled is worth +30 reputation instead of +15.

vote.label: Your vote
vote.vetoHint: Blocks the resolution: no effect applies.
vote.rules: A vote cannot be changed. It passes if yes outnumbers no; anyone who has not voted by the close counts as abstaining. Other countries vote at the close.

kindDescription.sanctions: Asks the world to isolate a nation economically.
kindDescription.peacekeeping: Asks for blue helmets to be sent to a contested region.
kindDescription.recognition: Recognises the legitimacy of a state or a government.
kindDescription.climate: Commits everyone to a climate accord.
kindDescription.nonProliferation: Bans new weapons of mass destruction.
kindDescription.condemnation: Formally condemns the actions of a nation.

propose.title: Table a resolution
propose.introCouncil: As a council member you can bring any resolution to the floor.
propose.introAssembly: From the assembly you can bring humanitarian aid and climate accords to the floor.
propose.reviewVote: Voting stays open for {weeks} weeks and your yes is already counted.
propose.reviewRule: It passes if yes outnumbers no. A veto from a council member blocks it.
propose.reviewEffects: A resolution you table has no automatic effect: what counts is the outcome of the vote, which stays on the record.
propose.reviewTreaty: If it passes the treaty comes into force: every warhead dismantled is worth +30 reputation instead of +15.
propose.pickCountry: Choose the nation the resolution concerns.
propose.pickRegion: Choose the region the resolution concerns.

veto.title: Cast a veto?
veto.description: A veto blocks the resolution whatever the others vote: it does not pass and no effect applies. It cannot be withdrawn.

error.notAvailable: The UN is not active in this scenario.
error.selfTarget: You cannot table a resolution against yourself.
error.notPermanent: That proposal is reserved to council members.
error.alreadyVoted: You have already voted: a vote cannot be changed.
error.vetoNotPermitted: Only council members can cast a veto.

cheap_power.name: Power almost for free
cheap_power.desc: The fusion reactor makes more than the grid can use. Households are waiting for their bills; businesses, for foreign markets.

pad_accident.name: Accident at the spaceport
pad_accident.desc: A launcher blew up on the pad. No casualties, but the footage is everywhere and the opposition wants everything halted.
pad_accident.a: Halt launches and open an inquiry
pad_accident.b: Carry on: this is how you learn

orbital_tourism.name: Tourists in orbit
orbital_tourism.desc: A consortium offers a fortune to fly paying guests to the station. The scientists aboard are not thrilled.

lunar_claim.name: Who owns the Moon?
lunar_claim.desc: A rival power disputes your base: the lunar south pole, it says, belongs to everyone. The world is watching your answer.

helium_rush.name: The helium-3 rush
helium_rush.desc: The first lunar shipment crashed the price of energy. Who collects: the state, or those who invested?

mars_silence.name: Silence from Mars
mars_silence.desc: The crew has not answered for nine days. Engineers say it is an antenna; the families, live on air, call it abandonment.
mars_silence.b: Wait: the signal will come back

mars_autonomy.name: Mars asks for autonomy
mars_autonomy.desc: A million colonists vote for a parliament of their own. They pay tax to a planet they will never see again.

type_one_day.name: Type I Day
type_one_day.desc: The planetary grid is live: for the first time a civilisation commands the energy of a whole planet. How should it be remembered?

belt_strike.name: Strike in the belt
belt_strike.desc: The asteroid miners have downed tools: eight-month shifts and nobody listening. Deliveries have stopped.

europa_life.name: There is life on Europa
europa_life.desc: Beneath the ice, something moves. Microbes, perhaps. It is the discovery of the millennium, and for now only you know.
europa_life.b: Classify it and study in secret

swarm_shadow.name: The shadow of the swarm
swarm_shadow.desc: The first Dyson mirrors take a sliver of light from Earth. Harvests are feeling it, and farmers have noticed.
swarm_shadow.a: Correct the orbits, whatever it costs

ark_lottery.name: Who boards the ark?
ark_lottery.desc: A hundred thousand berths on a one-way trip to Proxima. Ten million applications. Someone has to decide how to choose.

orbit.title: In orbit
orbit.text: Your nation has a home above the sky. Everything else starts here.

moon.title: The Moon is reached
moon.text: For the first time your flag flies on another world.

mars.title: Mars
mars.text: Seven months out, a whole planet ahead. Your civilisation no longer belongs to one world.

belt.title: The asteroid belt
belt.text: The resources of a thousand miniature worlds are within reach.

jupiter.title: Jupiter
jupiter.text: The giant and its moons: the farthest outpost ever built.

saturn.title: Saturn
saturn.text: Beneath the rings, a colony. The frontier moves again.

sun.title: The Sun
sun.text: You have begun to harvest your star's light at the source.

centauri.title: Toward the stars
centauri.text: The first step out of the solar system. There is no going back.

1.title: Type I civilisation
1.text: The whole energy of a planet at your command. Few hoped for it; you did it.

2.title: Type II civilisation
2.text: An entire star works for you. Your species can no longer go out by accident.

stats.title: How the run has gone
stats.empty: The record starts filling in after a few weeks of play.
stats.chartLabel: {name}: from {from} to {to}. Use the arrow keys to read values.
stats.table: Show the data as a table
